shared_elements: square/rounded glyph cartouches arranged in ordered rows and columns
anthropomorphic faces or heads enclosed within block-shaped cartouches
dense low-relief carving covering an upright monolithic slab/shaft
paired glyph blocks side by side reading in vertical sequence
curvilinear scroll and volute infill within cartouches
justification: Both surfaces are dominated by the same distinctive motif: rectangular glyph cartouches with rounded corners, each containing a face or head plus curvilinear scroll infill, set in a strictly ordered column-and-row sequence over an upright monument — a highly conventional and specific correspondence unlikely to arise independently. The main differences in depicted content are that B confines its glyphs to a narrow double column framed by dense foliate/serpentine ornament and includes a seated human figure and fallen debris at the base, whereas A shows a plain unframed four-column grid filling the whole face.
